# SolarSized

> Free solar and battery sizing: daily kWh to panel watts, battery kWh and inverter size, using NREL PVWatts peak sun hours by state.

Panel W = daily Wh / (sun hours x 0.75). Battery kWh = daily Wh x days / (0.9 x 0.9).

## Start here
- [Calculator](https://solarsized.com/)
- [Methodology](https://solarsized.com/methodology/)
- [About SolarSized](https://solarsized.com/about/): who publishes the site (EYEVUE Ventures), how the numbers are made, contact eyevueventures@gmail.com.
- [Privacy policy](https://solarsized.com/privacy/): cookieless Cloudflare Web Analytics, no accounts; an optional real-world test submission form (data + proof photo/link stored in Cloudflare, email optional and never published), affiliate cookies set only on the retailer's site, no sale of data. Effective 2026-10-27.
- [Submit a real-world test](https://solarsized.com/submit-test/): readers send measured solar production in kWh by system size and location with a photo or proof link. Every entry is reviewed by hand; verified results are published as "Verified owner test" data.
- [Affiliate disclosure](https://solarsized.com/disclosure/): Amazon Associates links, labeled and marked rel="sponsored".
- [Peak sun hours by state](https://solarsized.com/states/)
- [Appliances](https://solarsized.com/appliances/)
- [Data: states.json](https://solarsized.com/data/states.json)

## Guides
- [How many solar panels do I need? State-by-state sizing guide](https://solarsized.com/guides/how-many-solar-panels-do-i-need/): The average U.S. home used 863 kWh a month in 2024. Divide your yearly kWh by your state's PVWatts output per kW: that is 10–27 400 W panels for the average home, depending on the state. Full table, worked examples, batteries and FAQ.
- [How much battery storage do I need? Home battery sizing in kWh and kW](https://solarsized.com/guides/how-much-battery-storage-do-i-need/): Size a home battery for kWh (how long) and kW plus surge amps (what runs). Essentials: about 4.5 kWh a day; average home: about 32 kWh. Outage tables, winter recharge, Powerwall 3 vs aPower 2 vs IQ 5P.
- [Solar for an off-grid cabin](https://solarsized.com/guides/off-grid-cabin/): Size an off-grid cabin for the worst month, not the average: use winter sun hours, add 2–3 days of battery, and keep a generator for long cloudy spells. LiFePO4 batteries tolerate daily cycling best.
- [RV solar and battery sizing](https://solarsized.com/guides/rv-solar/): RV systems are limited by roof space: 400–800 W of panels is typical. Size the battery for overnight loads, and remember a rooftop AC usually needs shore power or a generator.
- [Grid-tie vs battery backup](https://solarsized.com/guides/grid-tie-vs-backup/): A grid-tie system without a battery shuts off during an outage for lineworker safety. Backup requires a hybrid inverter and battery, or a separate backup system, installed with a transfer switch by a licensed electrician.
- [Battery chemistry: LiFePO4 vs NMC vs lead-acid](https://solarsized.com/guides/battery-chemistry/): LiFePO4 is the default for home and off-grid storage: thousands of cycles, about 90% usable depth of discharge and lower fire risk. Lead-acid is cheap but should stay above 50% charge. NMC is lighter but ages faster.
